It touched 14 other cards around this alert and matches earlier confirmed cases on the same profile. It was found by pivoting from the card to the device profile and grouping every card on it.

case.summary: Alert HHF-001 opened because an analyst asked for a review of transaction 3660108 and related activity on other cards ($447.95, product C, online, 2017-01-14 20:25) on card C05061-K1. Assessed as an undocumented coordinated pattern with fraud probability 0.89. Main findings: The same template appears on 14 other cards within 14 days, none sharing a device with this card: coordinated abuse across customers; Card C05061-K1 already has 3 confirmed-fraud closed case. The account key is not usable in January, so the precedent is read at card level, where it is weaker: on cards of this size an earlier confirmed case made a new alert about 3.9 times as likely to be fraud. The episode covers 3 transaction(s) totalling $2,189.02, and 14 other card(s) are linked by a repeated template of product C purchases of $200 or more in bursts from devices marked New behind an anonymous proxy, with no shared device. Actions: block card, create case, file report, monitor connected cards, escalate to analyst.

sar.narrative: This report concerns customer C05061, card C05061-K1, issued as a visa credit. Between 2017-01-12 and 2017-01-14, 3 transaction(s) totalling $2,189.02 were identified as part of one fraud episode, beginning with transaction 3660106. The activity took place online, product code(s) C, billing region(s) 264, 492, from device profile(s) RCT6303W87M7 Build/MRA58K | Windows 10 | ie 11.0 for tablet | 1920x1080; RCT6303W87M7 Build/MRA58K | Windows 7 | ie 11.0 for desktop | . The transactions were bursts of online purchases from devices new to the account behind an anonymous proxy, the same template appearing on other customers' cards with no device in common. The activity is assessed as an undocumented coordinated pattern: The same template appears on 14 other cards within 14 days, none sharing a device with this card: coordinated abuse across customers; Card C05061-K1 already has 3 confirmed-fraud closed case. The account key is not usable in January, so the precedent is read at card level, where it is weaker: on cards of this size an earlier confirmed case made a new alert about 3.9 times as likely to be fraud. The shared element (a repeated template of product C purchases of $200 or more in bursts from devices marked New behind an anonymous proxy, with no shared device) links this activity to 14 other card(s), including C00450-K1, C02342-K1, C03528-K1, C05704-K2, which indicates a common actor across cardholders. Earlier confirmed cases CC-5229, CC-2674, CC-2420 show the same pattern. The cardholder has not yet been contacted. The bank has recommended BLOCK_CARD, MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS and opened an internal case; the report is filed under R9, §3a.
